name: Task Resolution, Special Rolls, and Retrying Tasks

text.content:
Task Resolution and Special Rolls

Cypher uses a d20 to determine the results of most actions. Higher is always better. If you roll the target number or higher, you succeed. The player always makes the roll, whether the character is attacking or defending.

NPCs do not roll dice. If an NPC is hindered, the player’s roll against that NPC is eased, and if an NPC is helped by a circumstance, the player’s roll against it can be hindered.

A task’s target number is determined by its difficulty. Because the d20 cannot roll above 20, difficulty 7 or higher is impossible unless the difficulty is lowered.

Special Rolls

If you roll a 1, 17, 18, 19, or 20, special rules apply.

  • 1: GM intrusion. Something occurs to complicate the character’s situation. The GM decides the intrusion. When this occurs on a roll of 1, the intrusion is a special case and the GM does not have to award XP.
  • 17: +1 damage bonus. On a successful attack that inflicts damage, add 1 damage.
  • 18: +2 damage bonus. On a successful attack that inflicts damage, add 2 damage.
  • 19: +3 damage bonus or minor effect. On a successful damage-dealing attack, choose +3 damage or a minor effect. On another successful task, choose a minor effect.
  • 20: +4 damage bonus or major effect. On a successful damage-dealing attack, choose +4 damage or a major effect. On another successful task, choose a major effect.

The extra damage from a 17–20 applies only when the attack hits and would inflict damage.

Minor Effect

A minor effect is a slightly beneficial result appropriate to the task. The character or GM can suggest one, and both must agree. In combat, examples include damaging an object held by a foe, distracting a foe for one round, knocking a foe back, moving past a foe as an extra action, or striking a specific body part for a special effect. If the desired effect is very unlikely, the GM might require an additional roll.

Major Effect

A major effect is a particularly beneficial result appropriate to the task. The character or GM can suggest one, and both must agree. In combat, examples include disarming, impairing, knocking down, or stunning a foe. If the desired effect is very unlikely, the GM might require an additional roll.

Retrying a Task After Failure

After failing a task, you can attempt it again, but you must apply at least one level of Effort when retrying it. A retry is a new action and takes the same amount of time as the first attempt. Additional retries follow the same rule.

The GM can rule that a retry is impossible. The retry rule does not apply to attacking a foe in combat: a missed attack cannot be retried as the same attempt, although a new attack can be made on a later turn.
